notices.html: Apple picking is off almost everywhere this fall: Terhune has now confirmed no pick-your-own apples at all for 2026 after April's regional freeze, matching Battleview's total crop loss and Johnson's Corner Farm skipping apples entirely. Lee Turkey Farm is the one local exception still listing some apples, so call 609-448-0629 to check supply before driving over.
Clocks fall back overnight Saturday into Sunday: daylight saving time ends at 2am, so Sunday gets properly dark well before 5:30pm. Plan outdoor plans, and the drive home, for earlier in the day.

Polar Express train rides are on sale now for late November and December: both Whippany (Morristown & Erie) and Phillipsburg (Delaware River Railroad) have 2026 dates listed, so it's worth booking the weekend you want ahead of time.

blurbs.terhune: This weekend, Oct 31 and Nov 1, is the last weekend of Fall Family Fun for the season, 10am to 5pm both days. There is no apple picking at all this year, confirmed by the farm itself after this spring's regional freeze. Pumpkins are still available to pick and carve. Festival admission (corn maze, wagon rides 11am to 3pm, live music noon to 4pm) runs $19.95 online in advance or $24.95 at the gate, kids under 3 free. Call 609-924-2310 to confirm before you drive over.
blurbs.leeturkey: This weekend: still the local exception on apples, with some varieties reportedly still on the picking list, though supply is uncertain after the spring freeze, so call 609-448-0629 first. Pumpkins should still be available to pick, admission around $3 on weekdays and $5 on Sundays for ages 3 and up. Open Mon to Sat 9am to 6pm, Sun 2 to 6pm, and you need to be in the fields by 5:15pm.
blurbs.vonthun: Von Thun's ticketed Fall Festival Weekends have wrapped up by late October in past years, so this Halloween weekend may already be past the festival dates, with just the farm market and any remaining pick-your-own open. We couldn't confirm this year's exact closing weekend, so call 732-329-8656 before you drive over.
blurbs.emerys: This weekend: the corn maze, pick-your-own pumpkins, hayrides and farm animals should still be running, with past-season weekend hours around 10am to 5pm. Berries are long done for the year, so it's pumpkins and the pie counter now. Call the picking hotline at 609-758-8514 or check emerysfarm.com first, since weather can change the schedule.
blurbs.battleview: This weekend: still no apple picking at all, the farm's first total crop loss in five generations after April's freeze. Pumpkin picking (priced by weight, cash only) should continue, and the country store stays open daily except Tuesdays with their own cider donuts. Call 732-462-0756 or check their Facebook page before you go.
blurbs.johnsons: This weekend: an October news report confirms the farm didn't have enough apples to offer picking this year, so they planted sunflowers, sweet potatoes and popcorn instead, which should still be ready to pick. The corn maze, hayrides, gem mining, petting zoo and pumpkin and gourd picking should still be running. Call 609-654-8643 to check hours before you go.
blurbs.dinosafari: Still closed for the season: the 2026 Freehold run ended August 16 and no fall return has been announced. No need for a special trip until it's back next summer.
blurbs.sixflags: This weekend is the final weekend for Fright Fest and the daytime Kids Boo Fest, running through Nov 1. Daytime trick-or-treating, games and a costume contest are fine for kids 9 to 10, but evening haunted mazes and scare zones lean older and start after dark. Go earlier in the day if that's a concern.
blurbs.diggerland: This is the last weekend for Dig or Treat trick-or-treating among the machines, running from opening until 12:30pm, with a costumed Parade of Machines around 1pm both days. The wider Diggerfest continues through Nov 15, included with general admission. Weekends only this time of year.
blurbs.sesame: This is the final weekend for The Count's Halloween Spooktacular, with the costume contest landing on Halloween itself, Saturday Oct 31. Trick-or-treating, a parade and dance parties continue on operating days through Sunday Nov 1. Hours vary by day, so check the park calendar first.
blurbs.lsc: Regular weekend hours continue, 10am to 5pm, still the biggest planetarium in the hemisphere. Book timed tickets online first.
